flexyBayes: Bayesian Mixed Models with ASReml Syntax via INLA and brms

Source: R/flexyBayes-package.R
flexyBayes-package.Rd

flexyBayes lets you fit Bayesian mixed models using the formula syntax you already know from ASReml or lme4/brms, dispatched through one of two active inference engines: INLA (integrated nested Laplace approximation, over the latent Gaussian model class) or brms (a Stan passthrough, full Hamiltonian Monte Carlo). A backend request naming any other engine refuses with an unknown-backend error naming the two active engines. All current exports are at the experimental lifecycle stage. The same fitted object supports summary(), predict(), emmeans::emmeans(), marginaleffects::predictions(), and the bayesplot::* family.

Entry points

The entry points share a single internal model representation (fb_terms):

  • flexybayes(), ASReml-format entry: fixed / random / residual formulas and known_matrices for kinship / pedigree. Observation weights are lowered for the Gaussian family (identity link) and refused by name for any other family, see ?flexybayes's @param weights for the exact semantics.

  • fb() / flexybayes(), the universal entry. Accepts an ASReml (fixed / random / residual) or brms-style (y ~ x + (1 | g)) formula, and any backend ("inla", "brms", or "auto").

  • fb_inla() / fb_brms(), the two active single-engine pins.

  • fb_prior(), penalised-complexity-canonical prior DSL.

  • vpredict(), ASReml's own verb for a posterior functional of the variance components: heritabilities, ratios and genetic correlations, computed on the draws, not by the delta method.

Vignettes

Six vignettes ship with the package: Mixed models in brief, Bayesian estimation in brief, The ASReml syntax flexyBayes covers, ASReml and flexyBayes on the same trials, A two-stage analysis of a series of trials, and Moving from ASReml-R. The first two set up the model class and what changes under a posterior. The third is the formula surface together with dispatch and the inventory of structures that are refused. The fourth fits the same trials through both and shows where the answers agree and where they do not. The fifth fits each trial of a series on its own, carries the first stage's variances into a second stage, and fits a penalised regression of trial-level covariates on the design whitened by the fitted covariance. The sixth gives the flexyBayes spelling of each ASReml construct, beside stored ASReml fits. The count here is checked against vignettes/ by a parity test, because a number written into prose is the first thing to drift.

Capability

What each active engine fits, emits, or refuses by model class is generated from one R-level table and shown in README.md and system.file("KNOWN_ISSUES.md", package = "flexyBayes"). A request outside that set raises a typed refusal naming the nearest implemented alternative instead of fitting a neighbouring model under the requested model's name.

References

Simpson, D., Rue, H., Riebler, A., Martins, T. G., & Sørbye, S. H. (2017). Penalising model component complexity: A principled, practical approach to constructing priors. Statistical Science, 32(1), 1–28.

Rue, H., Martino, S., & Chopin, N. (2009). Approximate Bayesian inference for latent Gaussian models by using integrated nested Laplace approximations. Journal of the Royal Statistical Society: Series B, 71(2), 319–392.

Gelman, A., Vehtari, A., Simpson, D., Margossian, C. C., Carpenter, B., Yao, Y., Kennedy, L., Gabry, J., Bürkner, P.-C., & Modrák, M. (2020). Bayesian workflow. arXiv 2011.01808.
